headline: 1996 executive order sets how the federal government manages export controls on encryption products.
what_it_does: This order deals with how the US government controls the export of encryption products, which are tools that scramble data so only authorized people can read it. It sets out which agencies handle these export rules and how they are administered. No summary was provided, so the specific details of the changes are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Companies that make or sell encryption software and hardware
who_it_affects.how: Their ability to ship encryption products to other countries depends on the export rules this order sets up.
The order directs how these agencies administer export controls on encryption products.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed November 15, 1996; the exact effective date is not stated in the provided material.
